mechanism: Both drugs inhibit CYP3A4 and possess anticholinergic/cardiac depressant properties; oxybutynin may increase amiodarone levels and both prolong QT interval through additive effects on cardiac conduction.
action: Monitor QTc interval, heart rate, and blood pressure closely; consider alternative anticholinergic agent with less CYP3A4 interaction; reduce oxybutynin dose if necessary and monitor for amiodarone toxicity signs.
